blocks.markdown: **TUESDAY | Choose Independently or Exclusively**

A JCheckBox is an independent on/off choice. A JRadioButton is one choice in a set; ButtonGroup makes the choices mutually exclusive, so selecting one clears the other. ButtonGroup controls selection; it is not a visible container. Add the buttons to a JPanel to arrange them [NTU] [BTN].
At a school materials desk, a learner may need both a guide and a practice sheet, but chooses one place to collect them. The selection rule is different from the arrangement of the desk.

blocks.markdown: **THURSDAY | Ask, Inform and Confirm Safely**

A JOptionPane provides a ready-made dialog, a small window that asks or tells the user something. Information reports a result; input asks for text; confirmation asks whether to proceed [NTU]. An input cancellation returns null; a closed confirmation returns CLOSED_OPTION [YORK-D].
A clerk can show a request, ask what to call it, or ask permission before clearing it. Silence, Cancel, No and closing a window do not mean permission.
**STEP 4 Ask, inform and confirm safely**

**Safe state changes:** acceptName checks null before trim; blank and over-30-character labels leave the previous name unchanged. The short-name limit keeps the request label readable. clearIfConfirmed clears subject/material choices only for Yes and retains the request name. Non-Yes outcomes report what happened.

**Modal:** a modal dialog waits for a response and can prevent interaction with its owning window until dismissed. That is expected. It differs from slow work freezing the interface. Keep sleep, join, await and slow file work out of listeners; retain ReadyTask’s background work and safe updates.

blocks.markdown: **FRIDAY | Your Own Theme: Interaction Task and Presentation**

An interaction is useful when a user can choose, act, understand the result and recover. Extend your own theme from Weeks 11–12 with purposeful controls, working model calls and honest tests. Keep useful nested panels and suitable layout managers [HWS] [NUS].
Arrange your own store, canteen, pet-care or school-service counter around what its user needs. Show what the user can safely change and what needs confirmation.

**Start Thursday after Step 4; present Friday.** Use your own theme, rather than copying Vehicle or submitting RequestDemo as your own work. Learn all four selection-control types and three dialog purposes; use only those that serve your task. Require at least two types and one appropriate dialog.
**Requirements checklist**
□ Extend your own theme; keep model rules and useful workers.
□ Use at least two selection-control types with clear purposes.
□ Combine inputs; reject missing, blank or invalid values.
□ Provide two different useful actions with working listeners.
□ Use at least one appropriate dialog.
□ Test every offered outcome; keep data on cancellation.
□ For input check null; for confirmation act only on Yes.
□ Keep nested panels, suitable managers, labels and feedback.
□ Use EDT for controls; keep slow work off listeners.
□ Record tests, complete self-check and present your own code.
**Five-minute presentation**
• Introduce your theme and intended user (30 s).
• Run one normal combined-input action (1 min).
• Prove bad input, recovery, a different action and safe dialog outcomes (2 min).
• Point to two controls, nested groups, a model call and the handler (1 min).
• Answer a question about your own code (30 s).
**Plan before typing | Teacher checks first**
**Testing evidence | Exact inputs and outcomes**

Record actual outcomes. If a check was unavailable, write “not tested” and explain. Include a failed test and the repair. Keep existing slow work off listeners; if your theme needs no worker, explain why.
**Two three-hour days**

**Thursday:** 100 min lesson/checks/strip; 20 min plan; 60 min development. **Friday:** 10 min recall; 50 min finish; 30 min tests/repair; 15 min rehearsal; 60 min presentations; 15 min slip/reflection.
For a large class: use parallel circles of up to 12, peer records and teacher rotation.
**A tested example to adapt, not submit**

Steps 2–4 show a tested school-service theme. A canteen could instead use an item drop-down and an independent “pack separately” box, with Preview and confirmed Clear. Retain its existing model rules; no new price or discount is needed.
**Starter fragment:** Open OwnTheme_fragment.txt in the performance task. It contains the printed blanks.
Fragment only, inside an existing method/listener. Fill choices/text, GridLayout and null; add labelled inputs and validate before a useful model call. Keep working model code.
